payload.summary: Reported by codex working on speed-count-game (its journaled note, run snqf4bfj, 2026-07-29T00:30Z), relayed by Jim: on the standing btze4m2j journal.divergence, validate --repair replayed ONLY the archived run.started into a fresh live run-btze4m2j.jsonl; the subsequent run end then rotated/wrote over the EXISTING archived run-btze4m2j.jsonl, deleting 10 prior notes — the CLI destroyed append-only history (HC6 violation) via its own suggested fix. Codex restored the three affected files from branch HEAD. Two distinct defects to investigate: (1) archive collision — rotation/write must NEVER overwrite an existing archive segment of the same name (refuse or uniquify, and validate should flag a would-collide state); (2) partial replay — repair materialized a record from an incomplete event set when the runs events span live + archive; it must replay across archives or refuse with a clear message. Repro likely: run whose segment was archived while its record lagged, then validate --repair, then run end. The btze4m2j divergence on speed-count-game is left standing on purpose — do NOT run repair there until this is fixed. Regression test must prove an archived segment can never be overwritten.
